subject: Science
summary: Subatomic particles are electron (e⁻), proton (p⁺), and neutron (n⁰). Rutherford discovered the small, dense, positively charged nucleus using alpha-particle scattering. Bohr proposed discrete non-radiating orbits (energy levels K, L, M, N). Bohr-Bury rule states shell capacity is 2n² and outermost orbit has maximum 8 electrons. Atomic number Z = protons; Mass number A = protons + neutrons. Isotopes share Z; isobars share A.

pages.heading: 1. Discovery of Subatomic Particles
notes: • Dalton believed atoms were indivisible spheres, but subatomic discoveries proved internal structure.
• Electron (e⁻): Discovered by J.J. Thomson (Cathode rays), charge = -1, negligible mass.
• Proton (p⁺): Discovered by E. Goldstein (Canal rays), charge = +1, mass = 1 u.
• Neutron (n⁰): Discovered by J. Chadwick (1932), neutral charge, mass = 1 u (absent in standard Hydrogen ¹H).

spokenLines.text: Welcome to class! Today we journey into NCERT Chapter 4: Structure of the Atom.
For centuries, scientists believed the atom was a solid, indivisible ball.
That changed when Thomson discovered electrons in cathode rays, Goldstein found protons, and Chadwick discovered neutrons.
Let us see how these three subatomic particles are arranged inside the atom.
Watch this animation of Rutherford firing energetic alpha particles at thin gold foil.
Most alpha particles pass straight through without any deflection, proving the atom is mostly empty space.
Suddenly, one in 12,000 particles rebounds directly backward — revealing the tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus!
Now interact with the shell model on the board.
Bohr and Bury established that shell capacity follows two n squared: K holds two, L holds eight, M holds eighteen.
Remember the octet rule: the outermost valence shell can never hold more than eight electrons.
Orbit around the 3D Bohr atom model on the board.
At the center sits the heavy nucleus holding protons and neutrons.
Electrons orbit strictly in discrete energy levels K and L without radiating energy, keeping the atom stable.

pages.heading: 5. Atomic Number, Mass Number & Isotopes
notes: • Atomic Number (Z) = Number of Protons = Number of Electrons in neutral atom.
• Mass Number (A) = Protons + Neutrons (Nucleons).  Notation: ᴬ_Z X.
• Isotopes: Same Atomic Number (Z), Different Mass Number (A). E.g., ³⁵₁₇Cl and ³⁷₁₇Cl.
• Isobars: Same Mass Number (A), Different Atomic Number (Z). E.g., ⁴⁰₁₈Ar and ⁴⁰₂₀Ca.

spokenLines.text: Here is your exam summary for atomic identities.
Atomic number Z tells you the protons, and Mass number A is protons plus neutrons.
Isotopes share the same chemical identity but differ in weight, while Isobars have the same total mass.

memorize.conceptTitle: Bohr-Bury 2n² Shell Rule & Mass Number Formula

memorize.expectedRecitation: Maximum number of electrons in a shell is given by the formula 2n squared, so K holds 2, L holds 8, M holds 18, and mass number A equals protons plus neutrons.

practice.title: NCERT End of Chapter Interactive Practice

questions.question: The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in the outermost orbit of an atom is _____.
questions.explanation: According to the Bohr-Bury scheme, the outermost orbit cannot accommodate more than 8 electrons (octet rule).

questions.question: Neutrons are present in the nucleus of all atoms except standard _____.
questions.explanation: Standard hydrogen (protium, ¹H₁) has 1 proton and 0 neutrons in its nucleus.

questions.question: Rutherford’s alpha-particle scattering experiment led to the discovery of the:
questions.explanation: The deflection of 1 in 12,000 alpha particles by 180° proved the existence of a central, concentrated, positive nucleus.

questions.question: Atoms with the same atomic number (Z) but different mass numbers (A) are called:
questions.explanation: Isotopes have identical chemical properties (same atomic number/protons) but different physical masses (different neutrons).

questions.question: Electrons radiating energy while revolving in discrete orbits would cause an atom to collapse.
questions.explanation: Under classical Maxwell electrodynamics an accelerating charge radiates energy. Bohr postulated that electrons in discrete orbits do not radiate energy, explaining atomic stability.
